author: Codex Designer rehearsal, 2026-11-10. Descriptions, proposals and guesses are agent text.
stage_status: Stages 0 and 1 rehearsal only. No sent ask, approval, waiver, stage completion, first-touch certification or ledger write.

root_draft.text: GelatinousSlime makes generosity dangerous: the colony can feed itself from a living landscape, turn its flesh into building material and safe food, and eat it to purge poison, while the same body slowly reads unprotected people and animals into itself. Fertile-looking ground takes cultivated fields back; resistant herds and partly absorbed arrivals show different ways of living on the body. Leaving early, taking the dry way home, or administering a deliberately toxic antidote can save a person; conversion itself never makes them hostile. The gene seeker makes the bargain deliberate: choose a gene, venture into an exposed current, bring home a perishable dose, and entrust a comatose recipient to someone who must administer the antidote. The chosen gene comes with an unchosen rider and a lasting social price. The Titanoslime gives the body a moving mouth: what it finishes swallowing is lost, feeding makes it permanently larger by default, and its harvested chunk becomes a short-lived bioweapon. With expensive technology, the archive can grow a dead person back from their last recorded touch, leaving a gap between that person and the life everyone remembers afterward. These connected promises need separate demonstrations, including the colony's ordinary work between the dramatic moments.

failure_modes: F1: The kind body becomes either free resources with a cosmetic fee or constant chores without a worthwhile gift; farm, native ecology and ordinary production never deliver the chosen generosity/identity bargain. Sources: design/RimMandrake/biome_experiences_2026-10-20.md; design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/the_slime.md.

F2: The player cannot make an informed expedition or rescue: unreadable deadlines, stale current marks, coma or swallowed-pawn clocks produce losses that feel arbitrary, while direct-effect proofs pretend the player path passed. Sources: src/RimMandrake/GelatinousSlime/Source/GeneSeeker.cs; src/RimMandrake/GelatinousSlime/Source/SlimeAlerts.cs; src/RimMandrake/GelatinousSlime/Source/Titanoslime.cs.

F3: The living archive tells a false story: returned people do not match their last touch, native/visitor distinctions mislead, or promised boundaries between campaign, slime, titan and liquid systems do not connect. Definitions and historical closures conceal unexercised behaviour. Sources: src/RimMandrake/GelatinousSlime/Source/ArchiveResurrection.cs; src/RimMandrake/GelatinousSlime/Source/SlimeVisitors.cs; src/RimUtinni/StructureInjectionsRUT/Source/VaultDungeons/CompFleshSeal.cs.

If the returned person leads, it centres the archive's identity gap. All retain the other built capabilities and their coverage. A correction rewrites dependent claims; no reply approves nothing.

asks.decision: 01. **ASK FIRST — What makes its kindness dangerous?**
asks.text: Which moment best carries “the price is who you are,” and what in the proposed root misses your picture?
asks.guess: My guess, not your answer: The early kindness should be real; the horror is that accepting it gradually changes what the colony regards as an ordinary, acceptable price. I recommend leading with the bargain rather than the giant.

asks.tree_effect: What changes in the tree: Your chosen story supplies the first showcase candidate and its concrete rejection case. It becomes showcase 1 only after a recorded owner pick. Later showcases must add different capabilities; remaining checks stay ordinary scenes, and interactions keep their own checks. Root approval is not a flagship pick.

asks.decision: 02. **ASK FIRST — Which story should we show first?**
asks.text: Which story should come first when you judge whether we understood this biome, and what failure there would make you stop the demonstration?
asks.guess: My guess, not your answer: B, with A next: it joins a chosen gift, an exposed journey and dependence on another person. I recommend that order because it puts a colony decision at the centre.

asks.tree_effect: What changes in the tree: If supply trips carry the cost, require a useful harvest/manufacturing cycle with protected and exposed workers. If medical staffing carries it, require a normal workday where staffing choices matter and treatment remains practical. If the bargain should become routine once mastered, the scene instead proves useful production and reliable protection without inventing a permanent emergency. The ruled field conversion and full colonist ladder remain.

review.why: Local evidence/wording check only; no fresh author-independent review performed.

asks.author: Codex rehearsal 2026-11-10
asks.decision: 03. A season of taking its gifts
asks.text: What should still tempt this colony to send people onto the body, and what part of that day's work should still feel costly?
asks.guess: My guess, not your answer: Harvesting and chosen genes remain worth leaving safety for. The cost is planning who goes, how long they stay and who can treat them afterward, rather than checking every pawn constantly.

asks.tree_effect: What changes in the tree: If individual urgency must be visible together, add a readable ordering/deadline requirement exercised with ordinary and injected clocks. If stages plus deliberate inspection are enough, require accurate stage and patient information, with no new overview requirement. If routine treatment should use normal medical work, acceptance must follow that actual order and queue rather than calling the cure effect directly. No answer changes the antidote's toxicity or invents an automatic rescue.

review.why: Local evidence/wording check only; no fresh author-independent review performed.

asks.author: Codex rehearsal 2026-11-10
asks.decision: 04. A fair chance to save several people
asks.text: Before choosing whom to help first, what must the player be able to tell about these people, and how much intervention should saving them demand?
asks.guess: My guess, not your answer: I should identify who will be lost first and issue a treatment order without opening three separate health panels; I should still have to choose and provide the friend and medicine.

asks.tree_effect: What changes in the tree: If starting commits the window, bind a mark to the ordered journey and test expiry during travel and work. If the current can outrun the worker, require visible expiry, an honest stop/reorder and a no-expiry control. If a missed window costs the device, require that cost to be stated before departure and prove no gene sample is also produced. None authorises remote extraction or a permanent gene stockpile.

review.why: Local evidence/wording check only; no fresh author-independent review performed.

asks.author: Codex rehearsal 2026-11-10
asks.decision: 05. Reaching a current just as it moves
asks.text: At that moment, what choice should the worker's journey leave you with: finish what was started, follow the new current, or bring the seeker home—and what should the failed timing have cost?
asks.guess: My guess, not your answer: A clear warning leaves me the choice to follow a fresh current or retreat with the unspent seeker. Lost time and exposure are enough; I would not spend the device without a sample.

asks.tree_effect: What changes in the tree: If earlier bonds are current legal/social relations again, define how conflicting bonds are represented and rejected combinations handled. If they are remembered claims, separate the returned person's recollection from present reciprocal relations. If ordinary RimWorld relations are sufficient, require a concrete result for this case and explain it, without adding negotiation machinery. This question does not waive the separately documented missing snapshot fields.

review.why: Local evidence/wording check only; no fresh author-independent review performed.

asks.author: Codex rehearsal 2026-11-10
asks.decision: 06. An old relationship meets a changed colony
asks.text: What should happen at their first meeting so the returned person's earlier life is true without silently deciding everyone else's present life for them?
asks.guess: My guess, not your answer: The returned person believes the old bond still exists, while the living partner's later life remains real. The conflict should be visible before any new commitment is forced.

asks.tree_effect: What changes in the tree: If the point is immediate incapacitation, bind the concrete loss of fighting ability, with an unaffected control outside the radius. If it is a continuing death clock, explicitly define its progression after leaving the burst ground and the antidote/drying controls. If the point is dangerous ground and lasting impairment, prove movement and later consequences without pretending every hit starts a lethal timer. Each answer keeps the harvested weapon, short shelf life and ruled resistance/cure routes; none gives the body intent or new aggression.

review.why: Local evidence/wording check only; no fresh author-independent review performed.

asks.author: Codex rehearsal 2026-11-10
asks.decision: 07. What the terrible weapon does to a fight
asks.text: After that burst, what change in the fight would make this feel like the terrible bioweapon you described?
asks.guess: My guess, not your answer: The group immediately becomes much less able to fight or escape, and surviving the contamination becomes an urgent problem. Its danger to nearby allies should be equally legible.

asks.tree_effect: What changes in the tree: If the encounter is ecological, require native/visitor differences to be recognisable and an arrival-to-dissolution story, without quest machinery. If rescue is central, require an actual treatment/escape route and readable urgency. If exploitation is central, identify and prove the particular reward and its cost rather than inventing a general harvesting system. The ruled neighbour-derived arrivals remain under every answer.

review.why: Local evidence/wording check only; no fresh author-independent review performed.

asks.author: Codex rehearsal 2026-11-10
asks.decision: 08. The stranger already halfway into the body
asks.text: What should that encounter make a player consider doing, and what would make it feel wrong?
asks.guess: My guess, not your answer: It first shows what the body is doing to outsiders. Helping or exploiting it is the player's choice, with no implication that the body sent it or that every arrival is a rescue quest.
